HEADER
Date/Time: 2027-09-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE); Samantha Ortiz (Redwood SE); Markus Reilly (Veritas VP Eng); Leah O'Connor (Veritas Infra Lead); Amit Sharma (Veritas Head of Security); Tara Mendes (Veritas Procurement)

- Agreement to run throughput benchmarks and to share SOC2/ISO docs; Redwood to send pricing and SOW draft.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Aaron Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — capacity uplift request, eu private pilot, security artifacts, and procurement next steps. is that still right markus? sorry, marcus? I keep saying marcus.
[00:12] Markus Reilly: yeah that's right, Aaron. this is Markus. we had our executive review last week and they asked us to firm up a plan to double steady-state capacity and add an eu private instance for data sovereignty. timeline is kinda tight, end of q4 ideally.
[00:28] Aaron Chen: got it. before we dive in, quick intros — sam will cover technical details and benchmark plan. sam go ahead — you on mute.
[00:36] Samantha Ortiz: hi all, thanks. i'll run through recommended cluster sizing, the private control plane options, and what we need from your network/security team to stand up the EU private pilot. there's a couple of tradeoffs — dedicated vs private VPC, latency impact, and kv cache warm-up behavior that folks miss. also note some transcripts may show K V cash — sorry that's an artifact — it's KV cache.
[01:02] Leah O'Connor: good to call out. our infra lead question is around network peering and egress. if we go private, do we need a direct connect, or can we do a VPN? also curious about the autoscaling window for burst traffic.
[01:17] Samantha Ortiz: short answer — both work, but direct connect (or cloud interconnect) gives a more predictable latency and stable throughput. for autoscaling, we recommend a mix: reserved baseline for steady-state and autoscale for bursts. the critical piece is the continuous batching and the way it affects per-token latency; if you tune the batching window too aggressively you can hit higher tail latency on short requests.
[01:40] Aaron Chen: Markus, can you remind us of current qps and peak patterns? the uplift calc we did assumes 2x steady-state plus 3x burst headroom.
[01:49] Markus Reilly: right now we're at about 380 qps baseline across us-east and us-west, with peaks up to 1.2k during end-of-day processing. those peaks are okay for short windows — about 8–12 minutes. our product team also expects more consistent traffic from new ml features so baseline will creep up.
[02:10] Samantha Ortiz: ok that's helpful. with 2x steady-state we'd target ~760 qps baseline and keep burst capacity to 2.5–3k. for EU private, we'd mirror a smaller footprint initially — roughly 30% of the baseline — to satisfy data residency for EU customers.
[02:27] Amit Sharma: on security — we need to confirm key management. do you support customer-managed KMS or HSM? and how are audit logs forwarded? also SOC2 scope — what evidence can you share?
[02:41] Samantha Ortiz: we support customer-managed KMS, both cloud KMS integrations and customer HSM for private deployments. audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via TLS syslog or S3 buckets with lifecycle policies, and we can provide an audit log exporter. regarding SOC2/ISO, we'll send the latest attestations; we can't share raw evidence but we provide the reports and a controls matrix.
[03:05] Aaron Chen: i'll put that in the next steps — send SOC2, ISO attestation, and a KMS integration note. tara, anything from procurement we should be aware of?
[03:14] Tara Mendes: yes — we need pricing for committed capacity (monthly tiers), plus options for a 90-day pilot for EU private. also need to understand cancellation terms and data deletion SLA after contract end.
[03:25] Aaron Chen: understood. we'll include committed pricing tiers and a pilot option in the revised quote. data deletion SLA — sam, what's the standard?
[03:33] Samantha Ortiz: standard is crypto-shred and deletion within 30 days for hosted. for private deployments we can meet custom windows; we need to lock those in the SOW and confirm retention policies on the control plane side.
[03:46] Leah O'Connor: also — latency goals. product wants p95 < 220ms for chat flows. can you hit that from eu regions if private there?
[03:57] Samantha Ortiz: yes, with a private EU deployment and local model variants we can target p95 under 200–220ms. we may recommend a quantized model variant and higher reserved capacity to guarantee that tail. note again batching behavior — small messages can be sensitive.
[04:17] Aaron Chen: there's also the question of fallback — if eu private is down, do you want traffic routed to hosted with additional data residency flags? customers sometimes prefer fail closed vs fail open.
[04:30] Markus Reilly: we need fail closed from a compliance perspective — can't allow eu customer data to leave region. is there an automated routing policy for that?
[04:38] Samantha Ortiz: yes, routing policies are policy-driven. we can set region-strict rules that will drop or queue requests rather than route them to non-eu endpoints. that impacts availability but meets sovereignty requirements.
[04:51] Tara Mendes: okay, procurement note — if fail closed causes downtime, we need a clause for SLA credits or an agreed-upon outage playbook.
[05:00] Aaron Chen: we'll propose language in the SOW for emergency fallback and SLA credits for region-level outages.
[05:07] --- (small cross-talk, pause) ---
[06:10] Samantha Ortiz: quick tangent — model caching and prefix reuse: if you have many session starts, the kv cache warm-up time will increase tokens-per-request. for throughput it's worth pre-warming if you can batch or reuse session ids. sometimes customers call this k v cash warm up in notes — apologies for the transcription oddities.
[06:35] Markus Reilly: noted. we'll check with product on session strategy.
[07:05] Samantha Ortiz: on benchmarks — we propose a two-part test: 1) sustained throughput at baseline for 1 hour to validate thermal and capacity stabilities, 2) spike test to 3x for 10 minutes to test autoscale and burst handoff. we'll run from your VPC peered environment to replicate real networking.
[07:27] Leah O'Connor: what's the expected telemetry? we need per-token latency, GPU utilization, and per-request tracing.
[07:34] Samantha Ortiz: we'll provide a benchmark report with per-token histograms, KV cache hit ratios, GPU memory/SM utilization, and a trace sample for requests that hit the cold cache.
[07:46] Aaron Chen: good. plan to run the bench week of Oct 11 — is that workable for your teams?
[07:52] Leah O'Connor: yes that's fine.
[08:00] Aaron Chen: great. procurement timeline — tara, you mentioned needing a pilot contract; what's your internal cycle?
[08:06] Tara Mendes: we can turn around a pilot MSA within ~7–10 business days once pricing and the SOW are agreed. final contract extension will take longer — legal wants a 3–4 week window.
[08:18] Aaron Chen: ok we'll aim to have pricing and SOW draft to you by Oct 5, that should keep you on track. next — any concerns about model variants or quantization causing quality regressions?
[08:31] Markus Reilly: product is worried about hallucinations increasing with more aggressive quantization; quality regression gates will be important.
[08:39] Samantha Ortiz: agreed — Redwood Optimize can run A/B against your eval set and we can pin rollout percentages. we'll include recommended quantization profiles and a quality monitoring hook to rollback if regression crosses threshold.
[08:53] Amit Sharma: for compliance, we need attestable logs of rollouts and who triggered them — can we get a forensic trail?
[09:01] Samantha Ortiz: yes, audit trail includes actor, timestamp, model version, and rollout percentage; that's part of the console exports. we'll show you a sample during the benchmark test.
[09:12] Aaron Chen: quick note — competitors: you mentioned MegaCloud AI and AtlasInfer? how are you comparing?
[09:19] Markus Reilly: MegaCloud AI gave a cheaper sticker for hosted, but they can't do private eu with customer-managed kms. AtlasInfer promised on-prem but had longer lead times and opaque pricing.
[09:31] Aaron Chen: understood — we'll highlight where Redwood meets sovereignty needs and gives clearer unit economics.
[09:37] --- (15 minute block in call, paraphrased, some exchanges about technical specifics, ports, firewall rules) ---
[24:50] Samantha Ortiz: firewall specifics — we'll need inbound service endpoints and a small set of egress to our control plane for telemetry. ports 443 and a few health-check endpoints. i'll share a network requirements doc.
[25:12] Leah O'Connor: also can you support private certificate trust chain? we run strict mTLS for internal services.
[25:20] Samantha Ortiz: yes, we can do mTLS and custom cert chains for private deployments. will include steps in the runbook.
[30:05] Aaron Chen: procurement / pricing — high level, what we propose: committed baseline for 2x capacity at a discounted unit rate, burst credits priced separately, and a 90-day EU private pilot addendum with a one-time setup fee. we'll send detailed numbers.
[30:22] Tara Mendes: please include cancellation windows and the data deletion SLA. also need a clear statement of support hours and escalation path for critical incidents.
[30:35] Aaron Chen: support hours and escalation path will be in the SOW. for critical incidents we provide 24/7 support on enterprise tiers and a named support lead for the pilot.
[32:00] Samantha Ortiz: i want to call out one more thing — model compilation and kernel selection: when you move to different hardware in eu, there can be minor perf deltas. we'll include a compatibility matrix and recommended kernels for the models you run.
[32:18] Markus Reilly: good. can we get an estimate of performance delta? like 5–10% or more?
[32:24] Samantha Ortiz: typical is 3–15% depending on sequence lengths and the GPU family; we'll quantify for your expected workloads in the benchmark report.
[33:05] Amit Sharma: regarding audit: will you accept a 3rd-party pen test result and can we request a joint scoping call?
[33:13] Samantha Ortiz: yes, we can accept and will coordinate a scoping session. pravin is our security eng — i'll put him on the invite if needed.
[33:25] Markus Reilly: what's the SLO for model rollout regression? product wants an automated rollback under 0.5% quality drop.
[33:33] Samantha Ortiz: we can wire the monitoring to a rollback policy; 0.5% threshold is achievable programmatically.
[35:00] Aaron Chen: ok let's recap — action items: Aaron to send pricing and pilot SOW by Oct 5; Samantha to prep benchmark runbook and network doc and schedule tests week of Oct 11; Amit to send compliance artifact list by Oct 4. Tara will queue procurement items internally.
[35:20] Tara Mendes: yes, and also include a stub for the SLA credit language.
[35:28] Aaron Chen: any final Qs?
[35:33] Leah O'Connor: just one — do you have a recommended model version for eu? we run chat and embeddings.
[35:40] Samantha Ortiz: for chat and embeddings we'd suggest model v3-ig-quant for EU pilot — stable, low memory, good quality for embeddings. we'll include eval metrics.
[35:50] Markus Reilly: sounds good.
[36:05] Aaron Chen: great — we'll follow up via email. thanks everyone for the time.
[36:10] (call ends)
